ratings.excerpt: I have mixed feelings about this year's offering: an intermittently delightful yet unsatisfying rendition of Stephen Sondheim's Into the Woods. THE MATERIAL:

A flawed musical has been intelligently reclaimed as a late-summer night's dream that suggests fantasy is the first refuge of the psychologically damaged. … Of the three shows with music and lyrics by Stephen Sondheim and book by James Lapine, this has always been the most popular, and the most problematic. The stock charge is that a punchy first half is followed by a preachy second. … Timothy Sheader's dazzling revival solves the difficulty in two ways: by exploiting the scariness of the park after dark, and by seeing the action through the fevered imagination of a boy narrator. … Soutra Gilmour's design also brilliantly exploits the sinister beauty of the outdoor setting.

For all its faults, the strength of the company, Sheader's witty direction and, above all, the spectacularly-lit woodland location, ensure that this fairy-tale musical casts a pretty potent spell. … Timothy Sheader's outstanding revival … Mark Hadfield and Jenna Russell are both deeply touching as the Baker and his wife… Beverly Rudd is a chunky, spunky Little Red Riding Hood… THE CREATIVES:

Timothy Sheader's glorious production of Stephen Sondheim's intricate reworking of a handful of Grimm tales…  is spellbinding. … Sheader's fresh, attentive interpretation balances fantastical fun with a poignant sense of the nightmare terrors of childhood… His masterstroke is to replace the show's Narrator with a modern runaway boy, fleeing unhappiness at home. … Sondheim's score, gorgeously melodic and spikily rhythmic, sounds splendid and James Lapine's book is vividly realised in fine performances. … Mark Hadfield is a heart-warming Baker and Jenna Russell sublime as his Wife … Soutra Gilmour's ingenious scaffold set, with witty, expressive movement by Liam Steel, it is ravishing theatrical storytelling. … The inclusion of Our Little World, written for the show's London open
